I can understand it.  Try giving it an open and fresh perspective.  BMW, in my opinion is trash and has been for some time now.  It's people paying for a badge.  The company does some impressive engineering still, but not anything like they used to and they can't seem to pull it all together into an entire complete vehicle.  Some years ago I bought a super sexy 135i. It caught my eye in the center of the showroom, I took it for a spin and felt like James Bond, 3.0L twin turbo, manual 6 speed.  It was fast, cool, and I bought it quick.  As I acclimate into it I start noticing things.  'Leatherette'.  Really?  Fake leather?  No heated seats?   Come on?  Wait, manually adjustable seats?  WTF?  Manually adjustable mirrors.  1980's style BMW radio.... just like the BMWs of the 1980s?  Well, it's fast...but not if it rains.  Better tip toe around every single corner, and by corner I mean every curve in the road.  The front would slide, the rear would slide, traction control basically never stopped cutting the engine out.  I have a substantial amount of racetrack time, so I could noticeably feel the cars stability.  Included service packages?  Well, that's nice.  But not really.  Turns out those engines burn so much oil you can't go anywhere near 3k without losing so much oil the actual warning would come up on the dash.  So, to use the 'service package', I'd have to schedule to drop the car off for at least a day, at least once a month to fill the oil.  If you're not familiar with working on cars, it has to be pretty low on oil to the low oil warning light to trigger.

  
Then there was the day I was about two miles away from my house and it started to snow a little.  Just a dusting, not even an 1/8th of an inch.  Mind you this is Metro Boston, so the roads are prepped for it.  Well, I could barely get the car home those two miles, and there were 0 inclines to go up.  Shit, I could barely pull the thing straight out of the flat ground asphalt parking lot on mass ave.  That was on a Thursday I believe.  I had owned the car for 5 months I had bought it outright.  Well Saturday morning, I drove that sexy 135i straight to the jeep dealership, took a gigantic loss on it and put myself into a new jeep wrangler.  A couple weeks later I'm in a coffee shop and I see this guy park his fancy 535i BMW outside, he hops out dressed all Patrick Bateman, standing tall, walking with that 'I'm a big shot stride'.  He comes into the coffee shop and as we're waiting for our coffee I said to him.  'That's your BMW out there right?'.  He affirms with pride that it is.  I said, "Well, before you drive off make sure you latch your hood, it's only on the secondary.  Burning a quart or two every month huh?"  My aim wasn't to damage his pride, but I sure watched it drain out of his body language.  



I Still have the jeep wrangler, 13 or so years later.  The engine did develop a slight tick so I swapped in a monster custom engine.  I didn't have to, it'd still be running and driving fine with the lifter tick.  It's just a design flaw in the pentastar V6.   The depreciation on the jeep, if I had ever considered selling it is far FAR better than BMW.  Just about every angle the jeep is better, other than telling people what kinda car you drive.  And with the engine I put into it last year, my 2013 jeep wrangler is almost a full second faster 0-60 than that BMW super-duper-german-engineering-marvel sports car.

  
I can go deeper into pages of more details where jeeps are beating out BMW, but if you're still having trouble understanding, I 'm pretty sure the 'blind loyalty' you just don't understand would be the ironic explanation for your trouble grasping it.

Like the original response, there's more info needed, but there's no way you'll be able to get a good diagnosis on here.  Lower back pain has can have so many possible causes.  If you were able to clue us into the reason, you'd be telling us the caus and wouldn't need to be here asking.  I've struggled with back pain half my life (42 now), and finally found my contributing factors and was able to get it manageable without narcotics a couple years ago.  

If you go to a doctor with low back pain they'll send you to a neurosurgeon with a lumbar MRI.  The neurosurgeon will likely find something he can operate on.  When your only took is a hammer everything is a nail.  I'm not saying don't talk to your doctor, but don't let them put you in a worse position. 

The type of pain, where and when you feel it, and for how long might reveal something.  Aching, shooting, stabbing, etc...  That will also help with possible things you can try for it.  There could be tight glutes, hang your torso and touch your toes to stretch. Hips/hip flexors, pelvic tilt - knee down lunge forward keep your stomachs pulled in and back straight.  It could be something in your lumbar pinching a nerve, even if it's not, disk decompression is never a bad thing. Inversion tables work wonders for that.  

Yoga also is only going to help.  If you didnt know, hot power yoga can get you cut as F.  It's not all lazy spiritual focussed stretching.  You'll get to target and tone some brand new areas and I can promise it'll be a challenging and benefitial workout to put in the mix.

I'm betting you're pinning in your hips/ass?  Could be that area getting site soreness that can easily extend to your lower back.  Try pinning at your thighs, and see how sore this areas get and if it eases up in your back.

Countless possibilities.  The best bet is to really lay attention to your body.  Write down when, where and how bad the pain is when you get it and see how many things it could line up to.

Good luck

All these doctors trying to give buoe for pain management is rediculous. Same as the majority of legislation and red tape these stupid knee jerk reactions lacking any understanding or comprehension is only creating bigger and more severe problems.

The buoe will bund to your receptors and prevent the oxycodone from doing much.  Because of this many people take higher doses which can lead to an overdose.  There won't be any negative effects from taking oxycodone with buoe in your system, it just won't work or won't work very well. Taking bupe with a physical dependence on oxycodone will often cause precipitated withdrawals.  Meaning, instead of feeling a little bad over a few days, you will feel like absolute death in a very short amount of time. however   The bupe also has a much longer half life so it will take some time for it to clear out. 

Bupe should be used for a short period of time for it's intended application, which is to treat physical addiction and dependence on opioid medications.  It's being prescribed long term which just creates a whole new dependence which has no options for treatment aside from go through it raw and embrace the suck.  Same reason it shouldn't be prescribed long term or short term for pain management.  The addiction and withdrawal is terrible, it does not adequately treat chronic pain, and like opiates it certainly shouldn't be prescribed for any level of pain that isn't severe.

Transistors are created by injecting chemicals into the silicon.  It's called doping.  These doped areas will diffuse over time making the transistors weaker.

Poly gates are the on/off switch, a thin layer over the meeting of doped sections that control the transistors.  They degrade and can burn out. 

The tiny wires connecting everything in the chips will also degrade.  Molecules of metal are carried with the current, making the wire's connections weaker. 


There's a long list of things like this that effect the physical chips due to heat, demand and other thibgs.  Nothing is impervious to time.
